Tech Scan: Delivery

How can a team move an approved change into production while preserving evidence, authority and a way back?

Draft research reference; vendor documentation describes capabilities, not a locally tested delivery system.

On this page
Define the release boundaryChoose a delivery pathControl and record the releaseMonitor and recoverSources

Define the release boundary

Delivery covers the path from an approved pull request (PR) through build, promotion, deployment, operational observation and recovery. Workflows & factories owns the issue-to-PR handoff. Verification supplies evidence about the change; a passing check does not authorise release. An authorised human makes that decision under the applicable path to production, which remains the local authority.

Merge accepts a change into a branch; deployment puts a selected build into an environment. They are separate decisions: a merge-triggered pipeline needs an independently enforced deployment gate if approval is required. A prompt or agent instruction is not that gate.

Choose a delivery path

AWS-first candidate: assess CodePipeline with CodeBuild for build and test, a manual approval action before production, and a deployment action appropriate to the target. CodePipeline supports source, build, test, approval and deploy actions; an approval action pauses execution for an authorised decision.[1][2] This is a composition to pilot, not an established local deployment or an automatic safeguard.

Conditional alternative: where repository and CI already live in GitHub, assess GitHub Actions environments for the deployment gate. Required reviewers and self-review prevention depend on configuration and plan; self-review prevention concerns the person who initiated the run, not necessarily the person who merged the PR. Check the identity relationship separately and prevent bypass paths.[3]

Hard gates before either choice: confirm required capability, approved data location and retention, identity and authorisation, relevant model and API policy, security boundaries and a named operating owner. Record the evidence for each; if any gate fails or is unknown, stop and resolve it or seek an authorised exception. AWS preference does not override a gate.

Choose the deployment mechanism by target, not by habit:

Deployment target and mechanism
TargetDeployment mechanismNote
ECSECS-native blue/green first: a replacement task set on a separate target group behind the load balancer listener, with all-at-once, canary or linear shifting and a bake period holding both revisions.AWS calls ECS-native blue/green "now the recommended option for most teams and new projects"; CodeDeploy remains a valid option for existing CodeDeploy deployments.[5]
EKSKubernetes rollout or GitOps reconciliation (kubectl or Helm, Argo CD or Argo Rollouts).CodeDeploy has no EKS compute platform; its three platforms are EC2/On-Premises, Lambda and ECS.[6]
LambdaCodeDeploy: canary, linear or all-at-once shifting between versions through an alias, with alarm-based rollback.The one target where CodeDeploy is still the current default.[6]
EC2 or on-premisesCodeDeploy: in-place rolling update, or blue/green by provisioning a replacement fleet.Traffic shifts by instance count, not by percentage; the CodeDeploy agent runs on each instance.[6]

Build new pipelines as CodePipeline V2. Stage conditions (beforeEntry, onSuccess, onFailure), stage rollback, entry conditions with a Skip result and automatic retry on stage failure are V2-only; a V1 pipeline still runs but cannot use those gates. Use a V2 onSuccess condition with a CloudWatch alarm rule and a Rollback result to roll a stage back when a post-deployment alarm fires.[7]

Control and record the release

The release approver compares the exact build with the PR, independent verification results, outstanding risks and local release criteria. Missing, failed or mismatched evidence stops promotion for investigation; a new or changed build requires evidence for that build. The pipeline enforces the configured gate; a person interprets the evidence and accepts or rejects release.

Keep a release record linking the source commit and PR, immutable artefact identity such as an image digest rather than a mutable tag, build and pipeline execution, test and evaluation results, merge and deployment approvers and times, deployment target and strategy, configuration and flag versions, and rollback target. For AI-generated changes, also retain the model and prompt or skill revision when known; record unknown provenance as a gap, not an invented value. Store these links in the team's existing record, not an assumed new system.

Before adopting the candidate, the platform engineer tests in non-production that failed verification, missing approval and an agent identity cannot deploy, and that alternate credentials cannot bypass the gate. Record the expected and observed result and have the accountable owner resolve failures before production use.

Monitor and recover

The service owner chooses user-facing health signals, thresholds and an observation window before release; the on-call engineer interprets telemetry and decides when to intervene. Configure alarms and a tested rollback route for the selected target. For CodeDeploy, rollback can be configured for deployment failure or a monitoring threshold; it redeploys a previous revision as a new deployment, and does not undo every side effect of earlier scripts.[4] Plan separately for data migrations, configuration and irreversible effects.

Record the deployment outcome, signal links, incidents and recovery actions against the release. If health degrades or evidence is inconclusive, stop promotion, involve the on-call engineer and follow the tested recovery plan. No local pilot or representative-reader study has verified this reference.

Instrument with OpenTelemetry, not the X-Ray SDKs. The X-Ray SDKs and daemon entered maintenance mode on 25 February 2026, with releases limited to security fixes; AWS recommends OpenTelemetry SDKs or the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT), collected by the ADOT Collector or the CloudWatch agent, with traces still stored in X-Ray. Do not start new instrumentation on the X-Ray SDKs or daemon. No end-of-support date for the X-Ray SDKs is asserted here. For health signals, use CloudWatch alarms and CloudWatch Application Signals service-level objectives (SLOs), which track availability, latency and faults per service; set few SLOs, tied to user journeys, and alarm on burn rate, not raw CPU.[8][9]

For incident response, do not start new work on Systems Manager Incident Manager: it closed to new customers on 7 November 2025, and AWS points new accounts at Systems Manager OpsCenter. Compose the replacement: a CloudWatch alarm or an EventBridge event automatically creates an OpsCenter OpsItem, and an SNS topic notifies on OpsItem changes for paging. OpsCenter tracks work items; it is not an on-call rota, so add a partner pager for rotation and escalation.[10][11]

AWS computes no DORA metric for you. DORA defines five software delivery metrics: change lead time, deployment frequency and failed deployment recovery time (throughput), and change fail rate and deployment rework rate (instability). The AWS-published route is a blueprint, not a managed service: Argo emits deployment events, Apache DevLake calculates the metrics, and Grafana shows them. Treat the metrics as measurement, never as targets: setting deployment frequency or pull-request counts as goals invites gaming.[12][13]

Do not start on retired products or superseded paths

Do not start new work on a product whose vendor has ended support, or on a deployment path AWS no longer recommends for new work. Use the replacement named in each row.

Retired products and superseded paths
Product or pathStatusUse instead
Systems Manager Incident ManagerClosed to new customers 7 November 2025; AWS points new accounts at OpsCenter.OpsCenter OpsItems with a partner pager.[10]
CloudWatch EvidentlySupport ended 17 October 2025; the service was discontinued.AWS AppConfig feature flags.[14]
X-Ray SDKs and daemon for new instrumentationMaintenance mode since 25 February 2026; security fixes only.OpenTelemetry via ADOT or the CloudWatch agent, with traces stored in X-Ray.[8]
CodePipeline V1 for new pipelinesSupported, but stage conditions, stage rollback, automatic retry and entry conditions with a Skip result are V2-only.Build new pipelines as V2.[7]
CodeDeploy as the ECS defaultECS-native blue/green is now the recommended option for new ECS deployments; CodeDeploy remains a valid option for existing CodeDeploy deployments.ECS-native blue/green.[5]
Amazon CodeCatalystClosed to new customers; maintenance only.See the Workflows & factories do-not-use list, which owns this product.
Any release path that auto-merges or auto-deploys from an agent without a human approval gateA prompt instruction is not a control.A human approval gate in the pipeline or GitHub Environment; see Control and record the release.

Gaps and open questions

No managed service computes DORA metrics, keeps a single change record, or provides incident management for a new account. All three are composed from parts: Argo events into DevLake and Grafana for DORA metrics, pipeline execution history with CloudTrail and the GitHub deployment record for the change record, and OpsCenter OpsItems with a partner pager for incidents. The composition is the team's to own and audit.[12][13]

No release control understands "AI-generated" natively. No pipeline action, gate or dashboard distinguishes an agent-authored change from a human-authored one; the model, prompt and evaluation fields in the release record are carried as metadata by convention. That is the single biggest gap for this playbook's reader.

Whether any AWS-native service replaces Incident Manager's response plans and escalation for new accounts is unresolved: OpsCenter tracks OpsItems, and the rota and response-plan parts still need a partner product or a composed runbook.

Whether CodePipeline V1 will be frozen, or the console default changed, is an open question: no AWS statement to that effect was found. Do not plan a V1 exit on an assumed date.

The AppConfig managed-experimentation general-availability date was not re-verified here; confirm it against the AWS What's New post before asserting it. CodeCatalyst is assessed in Workflows & factories, not duplicated here.
